name: Combine multiple video clips into one MP4 with FFmpeg

parameters.content:
## Combine any number of video clips into one MP4 with FFmpeg (free, no API)

Upload two or more video clips - even mismatched ones, different resolutions, aspect ratios, frame rates - and get back one combined MP4. No API key, no account, no paid service: FFmpeg's `concat` filter does the real work, running for free on your own machine.

This is the clip-joining step from a larger faceless-video pipeline, pulled out on its own because "just concatenate these files" is one of the most common FFmpeg questions there is, and the naive approach (the `concat` demuxer) silently produces a broken or out-of-sync file the moment two clips don't share the exact same codec settings.

### How it works

1. A form takes two or more video files and a target output size (1920x1080 landscape, 1080x1920 vertical, or 1080x1080 square).
2. Every clip is saved to a per-run temp folder in upload order - that order is the concat order.
3. FFmpeg's `concat` filter (not the `concat` demuxer) is used: each clip is scaled to fit inside the target frame without stretching or cropping, letterboxed if needed, normalized to 30fps, and its audio is reformatted to a common sample rate - so mismatched clips still join cleanly instead of desyncing.
4. The combined MP4 is read back off disk and returned with a short report (clip count, output size).

### Setup

Self-hosted n8n only - this uses Execute Command, which n8n Cloud disables. Install FFmpeg on the PATH of the process running n8n, and start n8n with `NODES_EXCLUDE="[]"` and `N8N_RESTRICT_FILE_ACCESS_TO="/tmp"` - both are required or the file steps fail without a clear error.

## 1. Upload
Two or more clips, any resolution. Order selected = order joined.

## 2. Save each clip
One item per clip so every file writes to disk in a single pass.

## 3. Build the command
Scales, pads and reformats every clip to a common frame before joining.

## 4. Join + deliver
FFmpeg's concat filter joins them in sync, then the result is read back.

## Self-hosted only
Execute Command does not exist on n8n Cloud. See Setup in the overview.

nodes.name: Video clips and output format form
nodes.notes: Entry point. Downstream nodes read every uploaded clip's binary and the Output Format dropdown from here.

parameters.formDescription: Upload two or more video clips and pick an output size. You get back one combined MP4, even if the clips don't match in resolution or format.

nodes.name: Prepare Run
nodes.notes: Builds a per-run temp folder, lists every uploaded clip in selection order, and parses the target width/height out of the dropdown label. Requires at least 2 clips.

nodes.name: Create the temp folder
nodes.notes: mkdir -p is safe to run again. This wipes json + binary, restored in the next node.

nodes.name: Restore the uploaded clips
nodes.notes: Execute Command replaces the item with its own stdout/stderr/exitCode - re-attach every clip's binary and the paths from Prepare Run.

nodes.name: Split into one item per clip
nodes.notes: Turns the single submission (with N binary properties) into N items, each holding one clip - required because Read/Write File writes one binary property per item.

nodes.name: Save each clip to disk
nodes.notes: Runs once per clip item, writing every uploaded file to its own path in the temp folder.

nodes.name: Build the FFmpeg command
nodes.notes: Ignores the per-clip write results (just file metadata) and rebuilds the full command from Prepare Run's clip list - runs once regardless of clip count. Uses the concat FILTER, not the concat demuxer, so mismatched clips still join in sync.

nodes.name: Combine all clips (FFmpeg)
nodes.notes: Runs the prebuilt command as a single string. executeOnce=true since the command already covers every clip - this must not repeat per item.

nodes.name: Verify the combine succeeded
nodes.notes: Throws with the real FFmpeg error if the exit code was not 0, instead of silently returning a broken file path.

nodes.name: Read the combined video back
nodes.notes: Reads the finished MP4 off disk as binary output - the free-path deliverable, no external service involved.

nodes.name: Attach the combine report to the file
nodes.notes: Read/Write File's read operation replaces json with file metadata only - merges the clip-count/size report back in so the output has both the summary and the file.

main.node: Split into one item per clip
Attach the combine report to the file
